_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Stockport (Underbanks)
suggestions.editorialDescription: A Victorian market hall at one end and old bank vaults turned into wine bars at the other, with the steepest street in England running straight between them — the regeneration story every other northern town centre is quietly trying to copy.
suggestions.researchNotes: Genuinely distinct, well-known area check for this run: Stockport town centre's Underbanks/Market Place quarter is a real, widely-covered independent food-and-drink renaissance (manchesterwire.co.uk, stockport.gov.uk's own 'Six years that brought the Underbanks back to life' and 'Why everyone's going out in Stockport Town Centre now' pieces, Michelin Guide's own listing for Where the Light Gets In) — a Michelin-listed tasting-menu restaurant plus a genuine cluster of independent bars (The White Lion, Bruk, By Yon Orange, The Spinn Off, Odioba) around the historic Market Hall and Little/Great Underbank streets. None of this overlaps Cheadle Hulme (a separate, leafy, suburban Stockport-borough district several miles south, already covered) — the Underbanks is Stockport's own dense, urban, historic town centre, the kind of area a Manchester local would genuinely expect to see covered already. Coordinates (53.4112/-2.1564) verified against the Market Place, SK1 1EW postcode area. Metro assignment ('manchester', kind 'city') is a judgment call flagged for the reviewer: Stockport is its own Metropolitan Borough, administratively neither Manchester nor Cheshire, and was historically part of Cheshire before 1974 boundary changes (the same fact Cheadle Hulme's own entry cites) — but unlike Cheadle Hulme's leafy-suburban character, the Underbanks itself reads as dense urban regeneration (market hall, railway viaduct, DJ bars in bank vaults), closer in spirit to Chorlton/Ancoats/Northern Quarter than to Cheshire's county towns, hence 'manchester'/'city' rather than 'cheshire'/'county' despite the shared borough with Cheadle Hulme. accentColor is a deep brick-wine tone, checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent (closest neighbours are Chinatown's crimson-berry #A73F52 and Ancoats' rust-brick #9C5030, both notably brighter/more orange than this darker, more maroon #7A3B3E). No venues researched or suggested yet — this is a district-only proposal, same starting point Chorlton and Didsbury each had before their own first venue passes.
